rules.strengthAnchors: Keep main lifts through Nov 9 review. Retain longer if progress is good; do not rotate just for novelty.
rules.progression: Two explicitly confirmed successful exposures at the top of the rep range, same load/setup, 2–3 RIR and no pain: add the smallest available load and return to the lower rep target. Unknown load or completion never earns progression. For holds, add 2–5 sec after two clean confirmed exposures before changing leverage.
rules.power: Power goes after warm-up and before strength. 2 exposures/week; low resistance, 3 crisp reps/side with 90 sec rest. Stop on slowing or lost form. Never turn the dummy lab into conditioning.
rules.endurance: Start with two 35-min steady sessions plus the easy Sunday walk. Do not jump to a volume target beyond recent capacity. Build toward 150 moderate-equivalent min/week: add 10-min brisk walks on strength days, then 5-min increases to a steady session after two comfortable confirmed exposures. Count only actual moderate/vigorous active minutes, not all warm-up, rest or class time.
rules.setup: Maximum 3 equipment areas/day. Initial setup is counted once per movement; later sets use prescribed rest to reset. Batch rack/cable work and set rings once.
rules.variety: Keep strength anchors. Rotate mobility and optional dummy-study themes daily across four stable options; avoid either of the previous two calendar days. Keep power/accessory/boxing changes on the existing two-week cycle. No extra volume or equipment for novelty.
rules.weeklyReview: Count only confirmed training. Look at strength, aerobic minutes, quality power exposures, mobility, and skill learning separately. No catch-up doubles or guilt streaks.
rules.feedback: BJJ class, boxing and strength add physical load. Slow dummy lab adds skill practice only. Unknown is not no. Check reports before every build; never auto-complete silence.

dummyLab.theme: Daily rotation of familiar technical positions
dummyLab.question: Weekly question: can I keep posture and connection consistent while changing position?
dummyLab.advance: Rotate the stable study themes rather than repeating single-leg entries every day. Use only familiar positions; choose visual study instead of an unfamiliar technique. User-reported class/lab questions may override a theme. No fast takedowns, submissions, conditioning target or assumption of live-class proficiency.

themes.name: SINGLE-LEG POSITION CHECK
themes.home: Study one familiar single-leg entry slowly. Pause at contact to check posture and connection; do not drive or finish forcefully into the dummy. Up to 3 slow reps/side.
themes.cue: Where can posture or connection be kept more consistent?

themes.name: ARM-DRAG CONNECTION
themes.home: Review a familiar arm-drag sequence slowly with the dummy, or study your trusted reference. Pause after the arm clears; inspect angle and connection. Up to 3 slow reps/side.
themes.cue: Can I keep a useful connection after the drag without pulling harder?

themes.name: GUARD FRAMES + HIP MOVEMENT
themes.home: Review familiar guard frames and slow hip movement on the mat or with the dummy. Freeze between positions and identify one place where the frame or distance changes. No speed target.
themes.cue: What changes when I create a little more space before moving my hips?

themes.name: TOP-POSITION CONTROL
themes.home: Review a familiar stable top position with the dummy. Pause to inspect base and points of contact; reset gently and compare. Study only, without hard pressure or submission finishing.
themes.cue: Can I explain which contacts keep the position stable while I move?

checkIn.question: Quick training check-in: what did you actually do—strength/endurance, BJJ CLASS (minutes + intensity), boxing, and/or slow DUMMY LAB (theme + discovery)? What felt hard or painful, how is your energy, and any class/time limits tomorrow? A one-line reply is enough.
checkIn.unknownPolicy: No reply → unreported, no progression, no invented fatigue or missed-session punishment.
